wiki_text: Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 3 expansion comprises seven midscale liquefaction trains (T04-T10) adding more than 10 mtpa. Commissioning progressed through 2025-2026: Train 1 of Stage 3 first LNG and Train 2 substantial completion in August 2025; Train 3 first LNG in September 2025 with substantial completion in October 2025; Train 4 substantial completion in December 2025; Train 6 produced first LNG in mid-May 2026 with substantial completion expected by summer 2026. The remaining trains were expected to reach substantial completion by the end of 2026. Trains were producing LNG ahead of full Stage 3 commercial completion.

topic: First LNG production and first export cargo (2026)
wiki_text: Golden Pass LNG (QatarEnergy 70% / ExxonMobil 30%) achieved first LNG production from Train 1 on March 30, 2026, and shipped its first LNG export cargo on April 22, 2026, aboard the 174,000 m3 QatarEnergy-owned carrier Al Qaiyyah - making Golden Pass the 9th U.S. LNG export terminal to ship cargo. The three-train project has a combined nameplate capacity of roughly 18 mtpa. Train 2 was targeted for in-service in the second half of 2026 (mechanically complete by year-end 2026) and Train 3 in the first half of 2027 (around Q2 2027).

topic: Train 4 & Train 5 FIDs and FERC/DC Circuit litigation (2025)
wiki_text: NextDecade reached a positive final investment decision and financial close on Rio Grande LNG Train 4 on September 9, 2025 (Bechtel issued full notice to proceed; Train 4 JV held by NextDecade 40%, Global Infrastructure Partners 36.9%, TotalEnergies 10%, GIC 7.9%, Mubadala 5.2%), bringing capacity under construction to ~24 mtpa. Train 5 FID and financial close followed on October 16, 2025 (NextDecade initial 50% economic interest, rising to 70% after investor return hurdles; Bechtel NTP; substantial completion targeted for Q2 2031), bringing total capacity under construction to ~30 mtpa. On the regulatory side, the D.C. Circuit's August 2024 vacatur of FERC's reapproval was revised in March 2025 to a remand WITHOUT vacatur, allowing construction to continue; FERC issued a final supplemental EIS on July 31, 2025 and reauthorized the project.

Sempra Infrastructure Partners reached FID on Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 (Trains 3 & 4, ~13 mtpa nameplate) on September 23-24, 2025, with incremental capex estimated at ~USD 12 billion plus ~USD 2 billion for shared common facilities. An investor group led by Blackstone Credit & Insurance - joined by KKR, Apollo-managed funds, and private credit at Goldman Sachs Alternatives - acquired a 49.9% minority equity interest for ~USD 7 billion, while Sempra Infrastructure Partners retained a 50.1% majority stake. Bechtel Energy received full notice to proceed. Commercial operations for Trains 3 and 4 are expected in 2030 and 2031. Combined Phases 1+2 nameplate is ~26 mtpa across four trains.
